concept.title: What does
concept.shortdesc: drafts the DITA topics for a new hardware generation from the topics you already have, and checks every draft against the DITA grammar and your house rules before a writer sees it.

conbody.p: Each new generation of a product needs a set of topics with the same structure as the last one and new values. Writers usually copy the previous set and edit it by hand, so labels drift and values get typed twice. does the copying with checks:

ol.li: It finds the sibling topics: the topics of the same type in the same place in the DITA map, for earlier generations.
It reads the new values from a launch facts file. Each value has a source ID and a unit.
It asks to fill a JSON Schema built for that one topic. The model never writes XML.
Python writes the DITA XML. Every value becomes a key reference, and every open question becomes a draft-comment.
The draft passes the DITA grammar, the house rules and a grounding check. A field that fails is revised up to times, and then becomes a question for a person.
Each draft reaches a writer as a draft pull request. can't merge.

conbody.p: You can use two ways. On , you draft the held-out TPU7x set and compare each draft with the page Google published. In , you open an issue and receive one draft pull request per topic.
